title: Spelling List 5
ruleLine: twelve of these fifteen words hide a vowel that is written down and never said.

tips.listen: Listen for the vowel you never say — that is the rule this week.
tips.boxes: Remember the rule — one vowel in this word is written but not spoken.
tips.reveal: The silent vowel is in pink. That is the part the test is looking for.
tips.plain: No silent vowel in this one — every vowel here gets said out loud.

chart.head: The a you never say
chart.note: ea and ai. The a is on the paper and nowhere in the sound.

chart.head: The u you never say
chart.note: ou. Every one of these is said uh, with no u anywhere in it.

chart.head: Silent on the end
chart.note: the e that finishes a word without being heard — and the ue that goes with it.

chart.head: No silent vowel at all
chart.note: port = to carry, and two the teacher chose. Say every vowel in these three.

words.sent: The tailor had to ___ his arm twice before cutting the cloth.

words.def: to try hard to do or achieve something
words.sent: Every runner will ___ to finish, even the ones who know they cannot win.

words.def: a practice or trial performance of a play or other work, for a later public performance
words.sent: The last ___ ran an hour late because the lights kept failing.

words.def: perceived with the ear the sound made by someone or something
words.sent: Nobody ___ the doorbell over the noise of the storm.

words.def: something bought or offered for sale at a desirable price
words.sent: The coat was such a ___ that Ana went back and bought a second one in blue.

words.def: a white, glassy, see-through ceramic; china
words.sent: The cup was so thin that you could almost see the light through the ___.

words.def: situated in the south, or facing in the direction of the south
words.sent: They drove until the accents changed and they knew they had reached the ___ half of the state.

words.def: a child, a young person, or a young animal
words.sent: One ___ in the front row asked a question nobody on the panel could answer.

words.def: showing rudeness and a lack of consideration for other people
words.sent: It is ___ to talk over somebody who has not finished a sentence.

words.def: to take away somebody's hope or enthusiasm
words.sent: One bad practice should not ___ anybody this early in the season.

words.def: able to be carried, usually because it is small and light
words.sent: The little ___ radio ran on batteries and went everywhere with him.

words.def: uncertain, indefinite, or unclear in meaning
words.sent: His directions were so ___ that we ended up three streets away.

words.def: a large, thin, flat case for loose sheets of paper such as drawings or maps
words.sent: She carried her drawings flat in a black ___ so they would not crease.

words.def: the state of being open to attack or harm, in body or in feelings
words.sent: Saying out loud that he did not know took more courage than hiding the ___.

words.def: dull and repetitive; lacking in variety and interest
words.sent: The drive was so ___ that every mile looked exactly like the one before it.
